deities: Sumatinath (5th Tirthankara; white marble idol on a silver throne)

history.period: 1468-1514 AD (begun by Seth Bhandasa Oswal; completed after his death in 1514)
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - Jain (Śvetāmbara) temple; keep-or-drop decision needed. Seth Bhandasa Oswal, a Jain merchant, began this three-storey red-sandstone temple in 1468 AD; it was completed in 1514 after his death. It is celebrated for frescoes narrating the lives of the 24 Tirthankaras, mirror work, gold-leaf paintings, usta art and carved pillars. Legend says 40,000 kg of ghee was used in the mortar instead of water, and locals claim it seeps through the walls on hot days (some sources date it VS 1521/~1464 during Rao Lunkaran). CONFLICT FLAG: one source (indiaairport.com) says it was built in 1514 by brothers Bhandeshwar and Sandheshwar and dedicated to the 23rd Tirthankara Parshvanath - most sources say Sumatinath, 5th Tirthankara (verify).

name: Bhandasar Jain Temple
town_description: Bikaner is a historic desert city in northern Rajasthan founded in 1488 by Rao Bika (verify), built around Junagarh Fort. The Bhandasar Jain Temple stands in Bada Bazaar in the old city, next to the Lakshminath Temple, about 2.5 km from Bikaner Junction.

travel.road: Bada Bazaar, old city; auto-rickshaw recommended for the narrow lanes.

visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:00 AM - 1:00 PM and 5:30 PM - 11:30 PM (visitplacesindia - verify). No leather items (shoes, belts, bags) allowed inside per Jain custom; entry free.
